preamble: We, the managers of the Showler & Friends Fantasy Baseball League, founded in 2009 as a keeper league among friends and family, adopt these rules so that every manager plays the same game, every trade is handled the same way, and every season is decided on the field. Where these rules are silent, the Commissioner decides.

s: The league is the Showler & Friends Fantasy Baseball League (“S&F” or “the League”), hosted on Yahoo Fantasy Baseball as “S&F Baseball.”
The League consists of twelve (12) managers, each holding one franchise.

The League is a free league. No entry fee is collected and no prize money is paid. A February 2022 proposal to make S&F a money league received 7 votes for and 4 against and was not adopted; the League remained free.
League announcements and off-season trades are posted on the League Hub and in the S&F Baseball Facebook group. League votes are held in the Hub’s Suggestion Box; a Hub vote is the official vote.

Each manager shall check and set his lineup, make roster moves, be available for trade talks, and respond when contacted. A manager who can no longer meet these duties shall tell the Commissioner, who will find a replacement and may place the departing manager on a list for re-entry.
A manager who intends to leave the League must notify the Commissioner before December 1 so a replacement can be in place before the off-season opens.
A franchise left unattended may be reassigned by the Commissioner to a new manager during the season. The first such reassignment took place in July 2014.

(a) A manager who finishes in the bottom three of the final regular-season standings in three consecutive seasons is placed before the League for a retention vote.
(b) Before the vote the Commissioner contacts the manager to confirm he wishes to continue. Each voting manager is then contacted privately; individual votes are confidential and only the totals are announced.
(c) The manager in question, the Commissioner, and any manager in his first season do not vote. A majority of the votes cast for removal removes the manager.
(d) A manager who is retained faces a new vote after each later season in which he again finishes in the bottom three. A finish outside the bottom three resets his count to zero.
(e) The Commissioner announces at the start of a season which managers are in an evaluation year.

A manager may add a co-manager, subject to these conditions: (a) the co-manager is not added to the Facebook group or the league website; (b) all trade negotiations go through the head manager, and a co-manager who negotiates trades outside Yahoo is removed; (c) the co-manager may make transactions and send trade offers on Yahoo; (d) the Commissioner may remove a co-manager at any time.

The Commissioner administers the League, enters keepers and off-season trades, sets the schedule and deadlines, and rules on every question these rules do not answer. Final decisions rest with the Commissioner.

Any manager may suggest a rule change in the Hub’s Suggestion Box, with his name or anonymously. The Commissioner decides which suggestions go to a vote. A vote stays open 72 hours. Every manager except the Commissioner may vote and may change his vote until it closes; seven (7) yes votes adopt the change. The Commissioner does not vote. He reviews the result before it is announced and may overrule it. The final decision rests with the Commissioner.

A rule change adopted during a season takes effect the following season or off-season unless the vote states that it takes effect immediately. Disputes over existing rules are raised privately with the Commissioner during the off-season, not in public during the season.
Each manager shall check his roster and draft board after every posted trade and before each draft, and report any error to the Commissioner.

From 2015 through the 2018–19 off-season, a three-member Rules Committee elected by the League for one-year terms beginning December 1 reviewed recommendations, with the Commissioner holding the final word. The committee did not rule on trades. It was discontinued beginning with the 2019–20 off-season, when recommendations moved to open league discussion under §3.2.

Each off-season belongs to the season that follows it. A trade made from December 1 through the keeper deadline is a trade of the following season (for example, December 1, 2025 to March 2026 is the 2026 season).

December 1 — Off-season opens; off-season trades may be submitted.
February — Annual Meeting (§4.3).
End of February — Keeper deadline (§7.3); the off-season closes.
Mid-March, Sunday — Draft.
August — Trade deadline (§9.7).
Second-to-last week of the MLB season — Championship ends (§11.4).

The League holds an Annual Meeting each February, ordinarily on the last Sunday before the keeper deadline. The agenda includes the season awards, recommendation discussions, the division draft (§11.2), and trade talks. Managers who cannot attend should be reachable by phone during the meeting.
Each team carries 26 roster spots: 16 starting spots and 10 bench spots. In addition each team has 5 injured-list (IL) spots and 2 minor-league (NA) spots.
C, 1B, 2B, 3B, SS, OF, OF, OF, Util; SP, SP, SP, RP, RP, P, P.
A player may occupy an NA spot only while Yahoo lists him as NA-eligible.
Each team must pitch at least 30 innings per weekly matchup. A team that falls short forfeits the pitching categories for that matchup.
There is no roster limit during the off-season. Only the eight keepers (and NA keepers) carry into the new season.
Head-to-head, by categories. Each category won is a win, each lost a loss, each tied a tie. Standings are by winning percentage.
Runs (R), Hits (H), Home Runs (HR), Runs Batted In (RBI), Stolen Bases (SB), Walks (BB), Strikeouts (K, fewer is better), Batting Average (AVG), On-Base Percentage (OBP).

Wins (W), Hits allowed (H), Walks allowed (BB), Strikeouts (K), ERA, WHIP, Strikeouts per nine innings (K/9), Blown Saves (BSV), Saves plus Holds (SV+H). Hits, walks, ERA, WHIP and blown saves are scored low.
Each team keeps eight (8) players from its roster into the new season.

In addition to the eight keepers, a team may keep up to two (2) minor-league-eligible players, defined as 151 or fewer major-league at-bats and 51 or fewer major-league innings pitched. NA keepers occupy the team’s 25th- and 26th-round picks. A team that keeps fewer than two uses the open round(s) in the draft.

Keepers are due to the Commissioner by 11:59 p.m. Central on the last day of February (midnight beginning March 1), unless the Commissioner announces a different deadline. Keepers are sent to the Commissioner by text or Facebook message with each player’s full name, and NA keepers designated as such.
A manager may submit keepers at any time before the deadline. Submitting keepers ends that manager’s off-season: he may make no further off-season trades.
If a manager has not submitted keepers by the deadline, the Commissioner sets that team’s keepers as the eight highest-ranked players on its roster by Yahoo’s O-Rank.

Once submitted, a keeper may be replaced only if he suffers a significant injury, is suspended, retires, or meets a similar unexpected circumstance. The replacement must be requested before the draft, by the time the Commissioner sets on draft day. No keeper may be changed after the draft.
A live snake draft on Yahoo, held on a Sunday evening in mid-March, with one minute per pick. Keepers fill rounds 1 through 8, so the League’s first live round is the 9th.
The draft runs 26 rounds. Rounds 25 and 26 are reserved for NA keepers (§7.2) and may not be traded.
Draft order is the reverse of final regular-season winning percentage across all twelve teams, regardless of division titles or postseason results. The team with the worst record picks first.

A weighted lottery among non-playoff teams, with bonus chances for the top three consolation finishers, was adopted by league vote in February 2018 and used for the 2019 draft. It was repealed in 2019 and replaced by the consolation champion’s division pick (§11.5).
Players and draft picks may be traded. A player may be traded in the off-season only if he was on the team’s final roster. Trades may involve any number of teams.
Picks in the next two drafts may be traded. Each side of a trade must receive the same number of draft picks it gives up. Rounds 25 and 26 may not be traded (§8.2).

From December 1 until his keeper submission, a manager may trade by agreement with another manager. Both managers (every manager, in a multi-team trade) must send the Commissioner the exact same trade, naming each draft pick by round and pick number. The trade becomes official when the Commissioner posts it to the Facebook group and updates the off-season rosters and draft boards.

Off-season trades of picks in the current draft are entered on Yahoo before the draft. Off-season trades of picks in the following year’s draft are re-entered on Yahoo after the draft, once that draft board opens.
In-season trades are made on Yahoo.
Any manager may vote on Yahoo to veto an accepted in-season trade within one day. Seven (7) veto votes reject the trade. A trade that does not reach seven votes processes automatically.
The in-season trade deadline falls in August on the date the Commissioner sets on Yahoo (August 6 in 2026).
A manager who declines an offer should say why, or counter it, so the other manager knows whether to try again.
Free agents may be added at any time, with no limit on acquisitions per week or per season. Dropped players clear waivers in two days; waiver priority is a continual rolling list.
Lineup changes take effect the same day (Yahoo “Daily – Today”): a player may be started until his game begins.
Each manager is responsible for his own transactions. A roster move made in error stands.
The League plays in three divisions of four teams, redrawn every year.

At the Annual Meeting the previous season’s champion, runner-up and third-place finisher each lead a division and draft its members in that order, snaking, for three rounds. Each leader names his division.

Each team plays its three division opponents four times each and every other team at least once; the remaining weeks are additional non-division matchups. The All-Star break week is combined with the next week into a single matchup.

Six teams qualify. The three division winners receive the top three seeds; the remaining three spots go to the best records. The top two seeds receive a first-round bye, and teams are reseeded after each round. The playoffs run three weeks, ending with the championship in the second-to-last week of the MLB season. A third-place game is played.

The six non-playoff teams play a consolation tournament. The consolation champion chooses which division he joins for the next season, taking his place at the start of the third round of the division draft in place of the third-round pick of the division he chooses.
A tied playoff or consolation matchup is decided by the regular-season results between the two teams, counted in total categories won. If still tied, the higher seed advances.
The champion receives the S&F championship banner.
Trash talk is welcome. Personal put-downs are not. Once a rule is applied or a vote is decided, managers accept the result and move on.
When MLB cancels games, the League cancels the fantasy matchups covering the same dates.

If a season cannot be played, rosters and draft boards carry over unchanged into the next off-season. The 2020 season was cancelled under this rule; the 2020 draft was never held, and any 2020 games played were an unofficial redraft.

history: Top six teams make the playoffs; draft order set by regular-season winning percentage, not postseason finish.
Off-season trading established: 8 keepers; players on final rosters and draft picks tradable; both managers report the trade to the Commissioner; multi-team trades allowed.
Early keeper submission permitted; submitting ends a manager’s off-season.
Keeper injury replacement allowed before the draft; unsubmitted keepers default to top 8 by Yahoo O-Rank.
Off-season opens December 1.
Two NA roster spots added.
League votes 6–5 to redraw divisions; three divisions of four.
League votes to play division opponents four times.
Challenge Option adopted for in-season trades: two challenges per manager per season; seven votes to veto; vetoed trade may not be re-offered without change.
Top three finishers pick the next season’s divisions.
Draft picks must be traded in equal numbers; no off-season roster limit.
Challenge limit dropped; protests filed privately through Yahoo, seven protests to veto.
Rules Committee created (three elected members, Commissioner chairs).
Trades process automatically after 24 hours unless seven written protests are received.
Weekly minimum of 21 innings pitched introduced.
League vote 4–3 lets deadline trades stand after a roster-spot error; going forward roster mistakes stand.
Draft lottery for non-playoff teams adopted by league vote.
Same-day (“Daily – Today”) lineup changes put to a league vote; now the league setting.
Retention vote for three straight bottom-three finishes proposed (Recommendation No. 5); later invoked as league rule.
Draft lottery repealed; consolation champion picks his division.
Rules Committee discontinued; recommendations decided by league discussion and the Commissioner.
Roster expanded to 26; round 26 not tradable. One NA keeper allowed in round 26. Trade veto changed to a private league vote, majority (six) to veto.
League votes to suspend the draft; the 2020 season is later cancelled.
2023 draft board opened for trading during the 2021 off-season.
NA keeper defined as minor-league eligible (150 AB / 50 IP or fewer).
Co-manager rules issued.
League votes to expand IL spots beyond three.
First retention vote held; manager retained 7–3.
Money-league proposal falls short (7–4); league stays free.
Second NA keeper approved, effective 2023–24 off-season; rounds 25–26 reserved.
Wins retained as a category; Quality Starts not adopted.
Innings minimum raised to 30; one RP starting spot removed (SP-SP-SP-RP-RP-P-P).
NA eligibility restated as 151 or fewer AB and 51 or fewer IP.
Veto moved to Yahoo league votes: seven votes within one day.
Playoffs moved up one week; championship ends the second-to-last MLB week.
Tiebreaker clarified: total categories won head-to-head, then higher seed.

Suggestion Box opens on the League Hub: rule suggestions (named or anonymous) and official league votes, 72 hours, seven yes votes adopt; the Commissioner does not vote, reviews each result and may overrule (§1.4, §3.2).
